A.explanation: Too small because it uses $\sin 40^{\circ}$ instead of $\cos 40^{\circ}$ for the horizontal distance from X to the weight.

B.explanation: Balances moments about X: $F$ acting at full length balances $28 \text{ N}$ acting at half length with lever arm $\cos 40^{\circ}$, giving about $11 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: Too large because it omits the half-length for the centre of the uniform rod and uses $28\cos 40^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: Too large because it equates $F$ to $28\cos 40^{\circ}$ divided by the wrong factor and ignores the $L/2$ position of the weight.

hints: Notice that $F$ is marked perpendicular to the rod at the far end, while the $28 \text{ N}$ weight acts vertically down at the middle of the uniform rod.
Take moments about the hinge at X so the unknown hinge force has zero moment and only $F$ and the $28 \text{ N}$ weight contribute.
The perpendicular distance for $F$ is the full rod length $L$, but the moment arm for the vertical weight depends on the horizontal distance $(L/2)\cos 40^{\circ}$.
walkthrough: Let the rod length be $L$. The uniform $28 \text{ N}$ weight acts at the centre, $L/2$ from hinge X. Force $F$ acts at distance $L$ from X and is perpendicular to the rod.
For equilibrium, the sum of moments about X is zero, so clockwise moment from weight equals anticlockwise moment from $F$.
Moment from $F$ is $F \times L$ because $F$ is perpendicular to the rod.
Moment from weight is $28 \times$ horizontal distance from X, which is $28 \times (L/2)\cos 40^{\circ}$.
Set them equal: $F \times L = 28 \times (L/2) \times \cos 40^{\circ}$. Cancel $L$ to get $F = 14\cos 40^{\circ}$.
With $\cos 40^{\circ} \approx 0.766$, $F \approx 14 \times 0.766 \approx 10.7 \text{ N}$, about $11 \text{ N}$. This is option B.
